drivingQuestion: By what signs is a kosher bird, grasshopper or fish recognised, given that the Torah states signs only for animals?
outcomeNote: A mishna listing signs, with three tannaitic additions recorded and not adjudicated.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ סִימָנֵי בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ מִן הַתּוֹרָה, וְסִימָנֵי הָעוֹף לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ, אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: כׇּל עוֹף הַדּוֹרֵס – טָמֵא, כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֶצְבַּע יְתֵירָה וְזֶפֶק וְקוּרְקְבָנוֹ נִקְלָף – טָהוֹר. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עוֹף הַחוֹלֵק אֶת רַגְלָיו – טָמֵא.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The signs» that indicate that «a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal» are kosher «were stated in the Torah, and the signs of» a kosher «bird were not» explicitly «stated. But the Sages stated» certain signs in a bird: «Any bird that claws» its prey and eats it is «non-kosher. Any» bird «that has an extra digit» behind the leg slightly elevated above the other digits, «and a crop,» which is a sack alongside the gullet in which food is stored prior to digestion, «and» for which the yellowish membrane inside «its gizzard can be peeled,» is «kosher. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says: Any bird that splits» the digits of «its feet» when standing on a string, placing two digits on one side of the string and two on the other, is «non-kosher.»

segments.he: וּבַחֲגָבִים, כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע רַגְלַיִם, וְאַרְבַּע כְּנָפַיִם, וְקַרְצוּלַּיִם, וּכְנָפָיו חוֹפִין אֶת רוּבּוֹ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: וּשְׁמוֹ חָגָב. וּבַדָּגִים, כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׁקֶשֶׁת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי קַשְׂקַשִּׂין וּסְנַפִּיר אֶחָד. וְאֵלּוּ הֵן קַשְׂקַשִּׂין – הַקְּבוּעִין בּוֹ, וּסְנַפִּירִים – הַפּוֹרֵחַ בָּהֶן.
segments.en: «And with regard to grasshoppers,» whose signs were also not stated in the Torah, the Sages stated: «Any» grasshopper «that has four legs, and four wings, and» two additional «jumping legs, and whose wings cover most of its» body, is kosher. «Rabbi Yosei says: And» this applies only if the «name» of «its» species is «grasshopper. And with regard to fish,» the signs are explicitly stated in the Torah: «Any» fish «that has a fin and a scale» is kosher; «Rabbi Yehuda says: Two scales and one fin. And these are scales:» Those «that» are «fixed to its» body; «and fins» are those «with which» the fish «swims.»

moves.cueHe: סימני בהמה וחיה נאמרו מן התורה
moves.summary: the Torah states the signs of animals but not of birds
moves.about: that the signs of a kosher domesticated and undomesticated animal are stated in the Torah, while those of a bird are not

moves.cueHe: אבל אמרו חכמים: כל עוף הדורס – טמא
moves.summary: the Sages supply the signs of a kosher bird
moves.about: the signs the Sages supplied for distinguishing a kosher bird — clawing, an extra digit, a crop and a peelable gizzard

moves.summary: a further disqualifying sign: a bird that splits its digits
moves.about: which signs mark a bird as non-kosher — whether splitting its digits on a perch is itself a disqualifying sign

moves.cueHe: ובחגבים, כל שיש לו ארבע רגלים
moves.summary: the four signs of a kosher grasshopper
moves.about: whether the four physical signs suffice for a kosher grasshopper or its species must also be called ḥagav

moves.summary: R' Yosei adds that its species must be named ḥagav
moves.about: how many scales and fins a fish must have to be kosher

moves.cueHe: ובדגים, כל שיש לו סנפיר וקשקשת
moves.summary: a kosher fish has a fin and a scale

moves.cueHe: רבי יהודה אומר: שני קשקשין וסנפיר אחד
moves.summary: R' Yehuda requires two scales and one fin
the mishna defines scales and fins
